Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the run chase. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Jatinder Singh and Aamir Kaleem walk in with their blades for Oman. Junaid Siddique has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
...THE CHASE...

Oman toiled hard for wickets and to stem the run flow. Till the halfway mark, they took the beating but Oman brilliantly pulled things back in the middle phase to get back in the game. However, they failed to stick to the process as United Arab Emirates once again found their rhythm to put Oman on the back foot. Oman bowled well in patches and also looked rusty on the field. It was not their best performance but they could turn things around by chasing this. It won't be a straightforward chase as the pitch is two-paced and will hope the top three make amends. Stay tuned for the second essay.

United Arab Emirates have surpassed the 170-mark but the way the openers were batting, it felt like they will touch 190. Alishan Sharafu and Muhammad Waseem struggled to get going but once they put on the skating boots, runs started to fly. The United Arab Emirates scored 50 runs in the Powerplay with Alishan Sharafu the aggressor. He fell right after his fifty while the skipper, Waseem, was dropped twice in consecutive overs when he was in his 30s, took his time before launching his fifty. His 24th fifty, which helped him cross the 3000-run mark in the T20Is as well.

A finish with a flurry by United Arab Emirates. 26 runs were scored in the final two overs, which replenished the idea of posting a big target. United Arab Emirates will be confident going into the chase, while Oman will hope they could have bowled a bit better in the initial phase.

A dot to end the innings then! Hassnain Shah bowls the wide yorker, outside off, Harshit Kaushik throws his bat at it but misses. However, there is a noise, as the keeper, Vinayak Shukla grabs it and appeals. The umpire says no, but Jatinder Singh takes the review. UltraEdge and replay confirm that there is no bat involved and the noise was from the bat hitting the ground. United Arab Emirates finish on 172/5!

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness now! It is really hot out there, and the spectators are countering the heat with caps, sunglasses, and sitting in the shade. Not ideal conditions for the players, but they will need to find a way to adapt here. We can now see the Oman players spread out and take their respective field positions. The on-field umpires pick up the match ball and make their way out to the middle along with the match officials. They are followed by the players from both sides, who line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Oman's first, followed by the national anthem of United Arab Emirates.

United Arab Emirates (Playing XI) - Alishan Sharafu, Muhammad Waseem (C), Muhammad Zohaib, Rahul Chopra (WK), Asif Khan, Harshit Kaushik, Dhruv Parashar, Haider Ali, Junaid Siddique, Muhammad Rohid, Muhammad Jawadullah (In place of Simranjeet Singh).

Oman (Playing XI) - Aamir Kaleem, Jatinder Singh (C), Hammad Mirza, Vinayak Shukla (WK), Wasim Ali (In place of Mohammad Nadeem), Hassnain Shah, Jiten Ramanandi (In place of Sufyan Mehmood), Aryan Bisht (In place of Zikriya Islam), Shah Faisal, Shakeel Ahmed, Samay Shrivastava.
TOSS - Oman have won the toss and elected to BOWL first.

Oman, meanwhile, also endured a heavy defeat in their opening match against Pakistan, though there were a few bright moments to take away. Their lack of experience against top-tier opposition was evident, but Aamir Kaleem and Shah Faisal impressed with the ball, and their spin attack looks well-suited to these conditions. Much like the hosts, Oman’s batting failed to fire, and skipper Jatinder Singh will be urging his side to learn quickly from their mistakes and execute their plans more effectively. The head-to-head record isn’t in their favor, with just one win in the last four meetings, but that will matter little if they can hold their nerve in the pressure moments - because in a game like this, that’s what will decide who comes out on top. Hosts United Arab Emirates entered the tournament on the back of a solid showing in the Tri-Nation Series against Afghanistan and Pakistan, but their campaign got off to a rough start as they were dismantled by India in their opening game. The batting lineup endured a nightmare outing and will need a swift turnaround to stay in contention. Much will hinge on skipper Muhammad Waseem and Alishan Sharafu, though they’ll need strong support from the rest of the order. With Junaid Siddique’s experience with the ball and glimpses of form from Haider Ali, UAE will be banking on a collective effort, and with the home crowd behind them, they’ll be hopeful of securing their first win of the competition.
